mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment above 0.3% for three consecutive months signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with INDPRO < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 3% for more than six consecutive months during a period of positive GDP growth (GDPC1) signals accommodative policy that supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% AND GDPC1 > previous quarter for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 3% and GDPC1 is rising for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -1% combined with a concurrent decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below -2% signals broad-based demand weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when GDPC1 YoY < -1% and HOUST < -2%.
